title: Fraud alert queue, June to September 2026

findings.headline: Fraud is concentrated in three alert rules
findings.detail: Confirmed fraud is 31.7% of Mule account inbound alerts (243 rows), 21.9% of New device + high amount (556) and 15.4% of Velocity (408). The overall rate is 10.4% (313 of 3,000).

findings.headline: New device + high amount hit rate is rising
findings.detail: Its monthly fraud rate went 18.1%, 22.1%, 23.6%, 24.3% from June to September. It also takes 15.2 minutes per alert on average, against 11.4 overall.

findings.headline: Two rules use a third of the queue for little fraud
findings.detail: Round-amount transfer (0.6%) and Night-time login (1.6%) make up 997 alerts, 33.2% of the queue (17.1% + 16.2%). Their fraud rates are far below the 10.4% average.

findings.headline: Fraud rate goes with amount and handling time
findings.detail: The top fifth of alerts by amount (from £34,533 up) is 19.8% fraud, against 3.7% in the lowest fifth. Alerts taking 15 minutes or more are 33.3% fraud, so long cases tend to be real.

findings.headline: Overall volumes and fraud rate are steady; data is clean
findings.detail: Monthly fraud rates stay between 9.7% and 11.1% on 694 to 793 alerts a month. There are no missing cells or duplicate rows. 89.6% of alerts are false positives.

next_steps: Review whether Mule account inbound and New device + high amount alerts can be prioritised or routed to the most experienced analysts.
Test whether tightening or merging Round-amount and Night-time login rules cuts workload without missing the small number of fraud cases they catch.
Check why analyst fraud rates range from 6.0% to 13.1%, starting with whether the mix of rules each analyst receives differs.

conclusion: The data is clean and the overall fraud rate is steady at about 10%, but fraud is heavily concentrated in a few rules, especially Mule account inbound, New device + high amount and Velocity. About a third of alerts come from two rules that rarely find fraud. First, prioritise the high-yield rules and then test whether the low-yield rules can be tightened.
limits: This review uses summary figures only, so it cannot show why rates differ, how much money was lost, or whether fraud that raised no alert was missed.
